# Quadrant brand guide

> Brand and style guide for Quadrant Labs and every Quadrant project. One system for people and agents: calm Chesapeake colors, a mark taken from a 1956 wooden sloop, plain precise writing.

Version 1.0.0, updated 2026-11-01. Canonical URL: https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/llms.txt
Human version: https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/ · Generated by _scripts/brand/build.py from brand.toml. Do not edit by hand.

Quadrant takes its name and mark from the Quadrant sloop, a 25-foot wooden boat designed by Laurence Hartge and built at Hartge Yacht Yard in Galesville, Maryland, in the 1950s. A quadrant is also an instrument for finding your position. That's the work: helping small teams find their bearings.

## Files

- [tokens.css](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/tokens.css): CSS custom properties (`--q-*`), light + dark. Copy into the project.
- [base.css](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/base.css): optional element defaults and classes `.q-btn`, `.q-btn-primary`, `.q-input`, `.q-card`, `.q-pill`, `.q-pill-signal`, `.q-kicker`, `.q-num`.
- [tokens.json](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/tokens.json): the same tokens for non-CSS tools.
- [assets/mark.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/mark.svg): Outline mark, ink. Light backgrounds.
- [assets/mark-reversed.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/mark-reversed.svg): Outline mark, white. Dark backgrounds and photos.
- [assets/mark-primary.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/mark-primary.svg): Outline mark, Bay Water. Light backgrounds, app bars.
- [assets/logo-horizontal.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/logo-horizontal.svg): Mark + wordmark, ink. Default logo.
- [assets/logo-horizontal-reversed.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/logo-horizontal-reversed.svg): Mark + wordmark, white. Dark backgrounds.
- [assets/favicon.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/favicon.svg): Filled mark, Bay Water. Favicons and anything 32px or smaller.
- [assets/app-icon.svg](https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/assets/app-icon.svg): Bay Water square with white mark. App and PWA icons (512px).

## Principles

When a rule below doesn't cover a case, decide with these.

- **Calm water, one buoy.** Surfaces are quiet: clean light backgrounds, deep Bay Water, plenty of space. Each view gets at most one loud signal, in buoy orange, on the thing that needs attention.
- **Made, not generated.** Use details that belong to Quadrant: the fan-shaped mark, Chesapeake colors, plain specific words. Avoid generic effects that could belong to anyone, like gradients, glows and sparkle icons.
- **Plain and precise.** Say exactly what is true in as few words as it takes. A number beats an adjective.
- **Same yard, different boats.** Every Quadrant project uses the same colors, type and voice. Projects differ by name and content, not by restyling.
- **Readable by everyone.** Every text color passes WCAG AA. Every product has a dark mode. Nothing is conveyed by color alone.

## Logo

The mark is the sail plan of the Quadrant sloop: a fan-shaped sector with a single bisecting line, tip up. The wordmark is QUADRANT in Jost 400, tracked +0.16em, converted to outlines. Always use the supplied SVG files and never retype the wordmark.

- **Assets.** `mark.svg` (ink, for light backgrounds), `mark-reversed.svg` (white, for dark backgrounds and photos), `mark-primary.svg` (Bay Water), `logo-horizontal.svg` and `logo-horizontal-reversed.svg` (mark + wordmark), `favicon.svg` (filled, for 32px and below), `app-icon.svg` (Bay Water tile).
- **Colors.** The logo appears only in `ink`, white, or Bay Water (`primary` in light mode). Nothing else.
- **Clear space.** Keep empty space around the horizontal logo at least equal to the wordmark's capital height. Around the mark alone, at least a quarter of its height.
- **Minimum size.** Horizontal logo: mark at least 24px tall. Outline mark: at least 24px. Below 24px, use `favicon.svg`, the filled version.
- **Orientation.** The tip always points up. Strokes are all the same weight.
- **Name in text.** Write "Quadrant Labs" for the company on first mention and in legal or contact contexts, and "Quadrant" after that. The wordmark always reads QUADRANT.

Don't:
- Rotate, stretch, skew, or outline the mark
- Recolor it orange, marsh green, or a gradient, or add shadows or glows
- Retype the wordmark in a live font, change its tracking, or set it in title case
- Put the outline mark on a busy photo; use the reversed version on a dark, quiet area
- Build a separate logo for a product (see Products)

## Color

Clear Day: the Chesapeake on a bright, windy afternoon. The palette has clear bay water, summer marsh and one signal-orange channel buoy. Use the tokens and never type hex values into product code.

| Token | CSS variable | Name | Role | Light | Dark | Contrast |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `paper` | `--q-paper` | Spray | Page background | `#F6F7F3` | `#0B1615` |  |
| `surface` | `--q-surface` |  | Cards, panels, inputs, tables | `#FFFFFF` | `#112120` |  |
| `ink` | `--q-ink` | Deep Channel | Body text and headings | `#10211F` | `#E8F0EC` | light 15.5:1 · dark 14.3:1 |
| `muted` | `--q-muted` | Heron | Secondary text: captions, hints, metadata | `#4E5E59` | `#94A8A2` | light 6.4:1 · dark 6.6:1 |
| `border` | `--q-border` |  | Rules, outlines, table lines | `#DCE2DC` | `#20332F` |  |
| `tint` | `--q-tint` |  | Subtle fills: chips, inline code, focus halo, selected rows | `#DDEEE9` | `#173230` |  |
| `primary` | `--q-primary` | Bay Water | Brand color as text or outline: links, secondary buttons, focus border | `#0B5E5A` | `#5FCFC3` | light 7.1:1 · dark 8.9:1 |
| `fill` | `--q-fill` | Bay Water | Brand color as a solid: primary buttons, progress bars, selected states | `#0B5E5A` | `#0F716C` | light 7.6:1 · dark 5.8:1 |
| `on-fill` | `--q-on-fill` |  | Text and icons on `fill` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FFFFFF` | light 7.6:1 · dark 5.8:1 |
| `accent` | `--q-accent` | Buoy (text) | Orange as text: emphasis, warnings, over-limit numbers | `#B8410E` | `#FF8A4C` | light 5.1:1 · dark 7.1:1 |
| `signal` | `--q-signal` | Channel Buoy | Vivid orange as a solid only: badges, alerts, one highlight per view | `#EE6A2A` | `#EE6A2A` | light 5.3:1 · dark 5.3:1 |
| `on-signal` | `--q-on-signal` |  | Text and icons on `signal` | `#10211F` | `#10211F` | light 5.3:1 · dark 5.3:1 |
| `secondary` | `--q-secondary` | Summer Marsh | Second data series, small marsh-green details. Not for text. | `#6E8F2E` | `#9DBE5A` | light 3.5:1 · dark 8.7:1 |

Contrast is the lowest ratio against `paper` and `surface` (text), or of the `on-*` color on the fill. Minimum 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for `secondary` graphics.

- **Fill vs. text.** Bay Water and buoy orange each have a fill shade and a text shade. Use `fill`/`signal` for solid areas, always with `on-fill`/`on-signal` on top. Use `primary`/`accent` when the color itself is text. Never set `signal` orange as text, and never use the light dark-mode text shades as fills.
- **Orange is scarce.** Use orange for at most one signal per view: an alert, an over-limit number, or the one badge that matters. Bay Water carries the brand.
- **Buttons are Bay Water.** Primary buttons use `fill`. Secondary buttons are outlined in `primary`. Orange is never a button.
- **Dark mode is required.** Every product supports `prefers-color-scheme` and lets the user override it with `data-theme="light"` or `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>`. `tokens.css` handles both.
- **Contrast.** Text passes 4.5:1 (WCAG AA), large text and UI boundaries pass 3:1. All text tokens are checked by the build, and the ratios are in the color table.
- **Charts.** Use series in this order: `primary`, `secondary`, `muted`. Use `signal`/`accent` only for the one series or threshold the reader must notice. Label series directly and don't rely on color alone.

Don't:
- Use cream, beige or parchment backgrounds; `paper` is a cool, clean light
- Use decorative gradients, including on backgrounds, buttons and text
- Set long text in `muted`; it is for short secondary text
- Add colors outside this palette, including for one product or one chart

## Typography

Jost for headings, so they match the wordmark. IBM Plex Sans for everything else. IBM Plex Mono for code. All are free on Google Fonts.

| Role | Font | Weights | CSS variable | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| head | Jost | 500 | `--q-font-head` | Headings only. Sentence case, weight 500, letter-spacing -0.005em. |
| body | IBM Plex Sans | 400, 500, 600 | `--q-font-body` | Body text and all interface text. 400 for text, 500 for labels and buttons, 600 for strong emphasis. Nothing heavier. |
| mono | IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 | `--q-font-mono` | Code, file names, keyboard keys, IDs. |

| Token | Size | Line height | Font | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `display` | 3rem (48px) | 1.1 | head | Homepage hero only |
| `h1` | 2.375rem (38px) | 1.12 | head | Page titles |
| `h2` | 1.875rem (30px) | 1.2 | head | Section titles |
| `h3` | 1.5rem (24px) | 1.25 | head | Subsections, card titles on marketing pages |
| `h4` | 1.25rem (20px) | 1.3 | head | App panel titles |
| `body` | 1rem (16px) | 1.6 | body | Paragraphs; keep lines under ~68 characters |
| `ui` | 0.875rem (14px) | 1.4 | body | Buttons, inputs, tables, navigation |
| `small` | 0.8125rem (13px) | 1.45 | body | Captions, hints, metadata |
| `kicker` | 0.75rem (12px) | 1 | body | Eyebrow label above a heading: weight 500, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.14em, `primary` color |

CSS: `--q-text-<token>` (size) and `--q-leading-<token>` (line height).

- **Load fonts once** with this URL: `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Jost:wght@500&family=IBM+Plex+Sans:wght@400;500;600&family=IBM+Plex+Mono:wght@400;500&display=swap`.
- **Headings** use Jost 500, sentence case, letter-spacing -0.005em. Never set headings in all caps. Tracked caps are only for the wordmark and kickers.
- **Weights.** Plex 400 for text, 500 for labels and buttons, 600 for emphasis. Never heavier than 600, and no italics for emphasis in UI.
- **Numbers** in tables, prices and metrics use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so columns line up.
- **Line length.** Paragraphs max out at 68 characters (`--q-measure`). Left-align text; center only single short lines.
- **Inline code** uses Plex Mono at 0.875em on a `tint` background.

Don't:
- Use Inter, or soft display serifs (Fraunces, Instrument Serif, Playfair Display); they read as AI-default
- Mix in other typefaces for variety
- Use light weights (300 and below) for body text

## Layout & components

Spacing is a 4px scale. Borders separate surfaces, and shadows are only for things that float.

Tokens: `--q-space-1` 4px, `--q-space-2` 8px, `--q-space-3` 12px, `--q-space-4` 16px, `--q-space-5` 24px, `--q-space-6` 32px, `--q-space-7` 48px, `--q-space-8` 64px, `--q-space-9` 96px; `--q-radius-sm` 4px, `--q-radius-md` 6px, `--q-radius-pill`; `--q-measure` 68ch; `--q-page-max` 1120px; `--q-shadow`; `--q-motion` 160ms ease-out.

- **Spacing.** Use the scale only: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96px (`--q-space-1` to `--q-space-9`). Page gutters are 16px on phones and 24px or more on larger screens. Content maxes out at 1120px.
- **Radius.** 4px for buttons, inputs and chips. 6px for cards, panels and code blocks. Pills (999px) only for status badges. Nothing rounder than 8px.
- **Borders, not shadows.** Separate surfaces with a 1px `border` line. Use `--q-shadow` only on menus, popovers and dialogs.
- **Buttons.** Primary: `fill` background, `on-fill` text, weight 500, 14px, padding 10px 16px. Secondary: transparent with a 1px `primary` border and `primary` text. Use one primary button per view.
- **Inputs.** `surface` background, 1px `border`, 4px radius. On focus, use a 1px `primary` border plus a 3px `tint` halo.
- **Focus.** Every interactive element shows a visible focus style. Never remove outlines without a replacement.
- **Motion.** Use 160ms ease-out for state changes only. No bounce, parallax or decorative animation. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Icons.** Use simple line icons with a 1.5px stroke (for example [Lucide](https://lucide.dev)) in `ink` or `muted`, at 16 or 20px. No filled, multicolor or 3D icons.

Don't:
- Build a hero that's a centered headline over a gradient, followed by three icon-and-blurb feature cards
- Use glassmorphism, blurred blobs or glowing borders
- Stack cards inside cards

## Illustration & imagery

Use real places and real things from the Chesapeake, wooden boats and navigation, drawn simply.

- **Illustration** is hand-built SVG or watercolor in the Clear Day palette. Good subjects are the Quadrant sloop, workboats, marsh, charts and tools.
- **Known exception:** the current quadrantlabs.io homepage uses a warm sunset watercolor of the sloop in an earlier palette. It will be repainted in Clear Day, so don't copy its colors into new work.
- **Photos** are real, in natural light, and credited. Only use photos we have permission to publish.

Don't:
- Use stock photos of people pointing at screens, shaking hands or high-fiving
- Use abstract 3D renders, gradient blobs or "AI sparkle" imagery
- Use emoji as decoration in product UI or headings

## Voice & writing

Quiet craftsman. Write like a good boatyard talks: plain, precise and warm, with no hype. Trust comes from specifics, not adjectives.

- **Say the specific thing.** Name the number, the tool, the outcome. "Deploys went from 40 minutes to 6" beats "dramatically faster deploys".
- **Short and active.** Use short sentences and active voice, and cut any word that isn't doing work.
- **Warm, not chummy.** Be friendly and direct. Don't use exclamation marks, "Oops", or jokes in error messages.
- **Nautical, lightly.** Use at most one nautical reference per page, and only if it helps the meaning. No puns.
- **Sentence case everywhere:** headings, buttons, menus, tabs.
- **Buttons say what happens:** "Save scenario", not "Submit" or "OK".
- **Errors say what happened and what to do next,** without blaming the user.
- **Empty states** use one sentence about what goes here and one action to start.
- **Numbers and dates.** Use numerals (3 clients, $14,200). Write dates like Nov 1, 2026 in prose, and use ISO format (2026-11-01) in code, file names and data.

Words that fit: help, build, decide, fix, plan, steady, clear, small team, part-time, course, bearings.

Words to avoid: elevate, seamless, unlock, empower, leverage (as a verb), cutting-edge, game-changer, supercharge, revolutionize, delve, journey, solutions (meaning services), synergy, world-class, best-in-class, "in today's fast-paced world".

- Marketing copy. Instead of: "We leverage cutting-edge technology to empower your team's journey to success." Write: "I help small teams decide what to build, who to hire, and what to leave alone."
- Error message. Instead of: "Oops! Something went wrong." Write: "Couldn't save the scenario. Check your connection and try again."
- Button. Instead of: "Submit" Write: "Save scenario"
- Empty state. Instead of: "Welcome to Planner! 🎉 Let's get started on your journey!" Write: "No scenarios yet. Add your first client to start."

## Products

Quadrant projects (Planner, Trip Split, Bookrec, Metronome and others) share the whole system. A product is identified by its name, not by its own colors or logo.

- **Naming.** Use the product's plain name followed by a small "Quadrant": **Planner · Quadrant**. Don't write "Quadrant Planner".
- **App bar.** Show the outline mark at 16 to 20px in `primary`, then the product name in Plex 600, then " · Quadrant" in `muted` 400.
- **Page title.** Use the form `<title>Planner · Quadrant</title>`, with the current view first when useful: `Scenario B · Planner · Quadrant`.
- **Favicon and app icon.** Use the shared `favicon.svg` and `app-icon.svg`. Products don't get their own marks.
- **Colors.** Products use Clear Day exactly. There are no per-product accent colors.
- **README.** The H1 is the product name. The first line says what it does in one sentence. The footer reads "Made by Quadrant Labs · quadrantlabs.io".

Don't:
- Design a product logo or wordmark
- Add a tagline under the product name
- Swap Bay Water for a "product color"

## For agents

This guide is written to be followed by AI agents as well as people. `llms.txt` contains every rule on this page as plain text.

- **Adopt in a repo** by adding the snippet below to the project's `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
- **Copy, don't hotlink.** Copy `tokens.css` (and optionally `base.css`) into the project and note the version from its header. Update deliberately.
- **Use tokens, never hex.** Write `var(--q-primary)`, not `#0B5E5A`. If a needed color doesn't exist, use the closest token and flag it. Don't invent a new color.
- **Use the SVG assets** for the logo. Never draw or retype it.
- **When unsure, choose the quieter option** and apply the Principles.

Snippet for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md:

```markdown
## Brand

This project follows the Quadrant brand guide.
- Rules: https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/llms.txt (read it before any UI, copy, or asset work)
- Tokens: copy https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/tokens.css into the project; use `var(--q-*)`, never raw hex
- Logo: SVG files listed at https://www.quadrantlabs.io/brand/#logo (never redraw)
```

Checklist before shipping UI, copy, or assets:
- [ ] Colors come only from `--q-*` tokens; no raw hex in components
- [ ] Light and dark mode both work; `data-theme` override works
- [ ] Headings are Jost 500 in sentence case; everything else is IBM Plex Sans/Mono
- [ ] At most one orange (`signal`/`accent`) element per view
- [ ] Primary buttons use `fill`, and there's one per view
- [ ] All text passes 4.5:1 contrast; focus styles are visible
- [ ] Copy has no words from the avoid list, no exclamation marks and no emoji
- [ ] Product name reads "Name · Quadrant" in the app bar and the page title
- [ ] Logo comes from the supplied SVG, at least 24px, in ink, white or Bay Water
